accessibility.title: Associate labels with form controls
accessibility.description: Form inputs must have programmatically associated labels.

accessibility.title: Do not use aria-hidden on the document body
accessibility.description: Ensures the document body is not set to aria-hidden, which would hide the entire page from screen readers.

accessibility.title: Enable keyboard navigation for all elements
accessibility.description: All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard with logical focus order and hidden elements excluded from tab sequence.

accessibility.title: Ensure all input fields have accessible names
accessibility.description: Checks that input fields have accessible names so screen reader users know what data each field expects.

documentation.title: WAI-ARIA 1.2: Accessible Name and Description Computation

accessibility.title: Prevent seizure-triggering flashing content
accessibility.description: Content does not flash more than three times per second to prevent seizures in users with photosensitive epilepsy.

documentation.title: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.1: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
W3C: Understanding SC 2.3.1 Three Flashes or Below Threshold

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for buttons
accessibility.description: All buttons must have a discernible, descriptive accessible name for screen readers.

accessibility.title: Provide alt text for image buttons
accessibility.description: Input elements of type='image' must have a descriptive alt attribute.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: Image Button state

accessibility.title: Support content reflow at 400% zoom
accessibility.description: Content reflows when zoomed to 400% without requiring horizontal scrolling or loss of functionality.

accessibility.title: Use logical heading hierarchy
accessibility.description: Headings follow a sequential structure (h1 to h6) that reflects the content hierarchy without skipping levels.

accessibility.title: Announce dynamic content with ARIA live regions
accessibility.description: Dynamic content updates are announced to screen readers using appropriate ARIA live regions.

accessibility.title: Avoid autoplaying media
accessibility.description: Audio and video content does not autoplay, or provides immediate controls to pause or stop playback.

accessibility.title: Avoid redundant entry in the same process
accessibility.description: Information already provided earlier in a multi-step flow is auto-populated or available for selection instead of being typed again.

accessibility.title: Avoid sensory-only instructions
accessibility.description: Instructions do not rely solely on sensory characteristics like color, shape, size, location, or sound.

accessibility.title: Do not disable pinch zoom
accessibility.description: The viewport meta tag must not set user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 as these prevent users from zooming in to read content, violating WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.4 (Resize Text).

documentation.title: Google web.dev: Does not have a <meta name='viewport'> tag with width or initial-scale

accessibility.title: Ensure ARIA attributes are valid
accessibility.description: All ARIA attributes must be valid and exist in the WAI-ARIA specification.

accessibility.title: Ensure ARIA roles contain required child roles
accessibility.description: Elements with certain ARIA roles must contain the required child roles or the widget structure will be broken for assistive technologies.

accessibility.title: Ensure content remains usable without CSS
accessibility.description: Content structure, instructions, and primary tasks remain understandable and operable when author CSS is disabled or replaced by user styles.

documentation.title: W3C: Understanding SC 1.3.1 Info and Relationships
MDN: HTML: A good basis for accessibility

accessibility.title: Ensure logical focus order
accessibility.description: Tab focus order follows the visual layout and logical reading sequence of the page.

accessibility.title: Include a skip navigation link
accessibility.description: A skip navigation link is provided to allow keyboard users to bypass repetitive content and navigate directly to main content.

accessibility.title: Keep focused elements unobscured
accessibility.description: Sticky headers, footers, banners, and overlays must not fully hide the element that currently has keyboard focus.

documentation.title: W3C: Understanding SC 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)

accessibility.title: Make modal dialogs keyboard accessible
accessibility.description: Modal dialogs are accessible with proper focus trapping, ARIA attributes, and keyboard dismissal.

accessibility.title: Manage focus during dynamic interactions
accessibility.description: Focus is programmatically managed during dynamic interactions like modals, page transitions, and content updates.

accessibility.title: Meet minimum color contrast ratios
accessibility.description: Text and background colors must have sufficient contrast to be readable by users with low vision or color blindness.

accessibility.title: Prevent data loss from session timeouts
accessibility.description: Users are warned before session expiry, can extend time when appropriate, and can re-authenticate or resume work without losing entered data.

accessibility.title: Provide accessible authentication methods
accessibility.description: Authentication flows avoid unnecessary cognitive tests and support assistive mechanisms such as password managers, paste, OTP autofill, and passkeys.

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for all interactive elements
accessibility.description: Checks that interactive elements have accessible names for clear navigation.

accessibility.title: Provide captions for video content
accessibility.description: Prerecorded video with audio must have synchronized captions.
accessibility.detail: Live video must have real-time captions. This is required by WCAG 2.1 SC 1.2.2 and SC 1.2.4.

documentation.title: WebAIM: Captions, Transcripts, and Audio Descriptions

accessibility.title: Respect reduced motion preferences
accessibility.description: Animations respect user motion preferences, avoid seizure-triggering flashing, and include warnings for excessive motion.

accessibility.title: Support both portrait and landscape orientation
accessibility.description: Content and functionality work in both portrait and landscape unless a specific orientation is essential to the activity.

accessibility.title: Support text resizing to 200%
accessibility.description: Text can be resized up to 200% without loss of content or functionality using browser settings.

accessibility.title: Test with screen readers
accessibility.description: Pages must be tested with actual screen reader software (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack) to verify announcements, focus order, and widget behavior beyond what automated tools can detect.

documentation.title: WebAIM: Using Screen Readers for Testing

accessibility.title: Use descriptive link text
accessibility.description: Link text clearly describes the destination or purpose without relying on surrounding context.

accessibility.title: Use unique IDs for active elements
accessibility.description: All focusable or active elements must have a unique ID attribute.

accessibility.title: Use unique IDs for ARIA references
accessibility.description: IDs referenced by ARIA attributes must be unique to ensure correct accessibility relationships.

accessibility.title: Align visible labels with accessible names
accessibility.description: The accessible name of a control should contain its visible label text.

documentation.title: W3C: Understanding SC 2.5.3 Label in Name

accessibility.title: Allow pasting into form inputs
accessibility.description: Users should be able to paste content into form fields to improve usability and reduce errors.

accessibility.title: Avoid focusable descendants in role="text" elements
accessibility.description: Checks that elements with role='text' have no focusable descendants

accessibility.title: Avoid meta refresh redirects
accessibility.description: Meta refresh redirects can disorient users and cause accessibility issues by refreshing the page unexpectedly.

accessibility.title: Avoid scrolljacking and custom scroll behavior
accessibility.description: Natural scroll behavior is preserved without custom scroll speeds, directions, or hijacked scroll events.

accessibility.title: Avoid using deprecated ARIA roles
accessibility.description: Checks for deprecated or abstract ARIA roles to ensure long-term compatibility.

accessibility.title: Define proper table headers
accessibility.description: Checks that data tables have proper headers

accessibility.title: Ensure accesskey values are unique
accessibility.description: Checks that accesskey values are unique to avoid shortcut conflicts.

accessibility.title: Ensure ARIA roles are contained by required parent roles
accessibility.description: Checks that elements with certain roles have required parent roles

accessibility.title: Ensure dialogs have an accessible name
accessibility.description: Checks that dialog elements have accessible names to orient screen reader users.

accessibility.title: Ensure headings contain text
accessibility.description: All heading elements (h1-h6) must have visible, descriptive content.

accessibility.title: Ensure identical links have consistent destinations
accessibility.description: Links with the same text must point to the same destination or be distinguishable.

documentation.title: W3C: Understanding SC 2.4.4 Link Purpose (In Context)

accessibility.title: Ensure table headers associate with data cells
accessibility.description: Checks that table headers have associated data cells

accessibility.title: Ensure tables have unique accessible names
accessibility.description: Checks that data tables have unique accessible names

accessibility.title: Fix empty and broken links
accessibility.description: All links contain accessible text content and do not lead to broken destinations.

accessibility.title: Hide decorative elements from assistive technology
accessibility.description: Decorative images and visual elements are hidden from screen readers using aria-hidden or empty alt attributes.

accessibility.title: Include required ARIA attributes for roles
accessibility.description: Checks that elements have required ARIA attributes for their roles

accessibility.title: Keep repeated help mechanisms in a consistent location
accessibility.description: When help or support mechanisms appear on multiple pages in the same flow, they stay in the same relative order so users can find them predictably.

accessibility.title: Link table cells to headers using IDs
accessibility.description: Checks that td headers attribute references valid th ids

accessibility.title: Maintain logical heading order
accessibility.description: Heading levels should follow a sequential, hierarchical order.

accessibility.title: Make links in text blocks visually distinguishable
accessibility.description: Links within blocks of text must be distinguishable from surrounding non-link text by more than color alone.

documentation.title: WCAG Technique G183: Using a contrast ratio of 3:1 with surrounding text
WCAG Technique F73: Failure for creating links not visually evident without color vision

accessibility.title: Match lang and xml:lang attributes
accessibility.description: The lang and xml:lang attributes on the html element must have identical values to avoid conflicting language signals across HTML and XML parsers.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The lang and xml:lang attributes

accessibility.title: Place list items within list containers
accessibility.description: List item elements (li) must always be direct children of a list container (ul, ol, or menu) to maintain valid HTML structure and correct screen reader announcements.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The li element

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for ARIA command elements
accessibility.description: Checks that command elements like buttons and links have accessible names for screen reader support.

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for meter elements
accessibility.description: Checks that meter elements have accessible names to provide context for measurements.

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for progress bars
accessibility.description: Checks that progressbar elements have accessible names

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for select elements
accessibility.description: All `<select>` elements must have an associated label or an accessible name to be correctly identified by screen readers.

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for toggle fields
accessibility.description: Checks that toggle fields (checkbox, radio, switch) have accessible names

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for tooltips
accessibility.description: Checks that tooltip elements have accessible names

accessibility.title: Provide accessible names for tree items
accessibility.description: All elements with role="treeitem" must have a descriptive accessible name so screen reader users can navigate hierarchical tree widgets.

documentation.title: ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Tree View Pattern

accessibility.title: Provide alternative text for objects
accessibility.description: The `<object>` element must contain alternative content to ensure accessibility for users who cannot view the primary content.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The object element

accessibility.title: Provide alternatives to parallax effects
accessibility.description: Parallax scrolling effects have reduced-motion alternatives or can be disabled by users.

accessibility.title: Provide audio descriptions for video
accessibility.description: Videos with important visual content include audio descriptions that narrate visual information for blind users.

accessibility.title: Provide sufficient touch target size
accessibility.description: Interactive elements must have large enough touch targets so users with motor impairments can activate them accurately on touchscreen devices.

documentation.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Adaptivity and Layout

accessibility.title: Provide titles for iframes and frames
accessibility.description: iframes and frames must have a title attribute to describe their content.

accessibility.title: Remove focusable elements from aria-hidden containers
accessibility.description: Ensures aria-hidden elements do not contain focusable content to avoid "ghost" focus.

accessibility.title: Use a single label for each form field
accessibility.description: Form fields should have exactly one associated <label> element for maximum clarity.

accessibility.title: Use appropriate tabindex values
accessibility.description: Checks for appropriate tabindex values

accessibility.title: Use correct definition list structure
accessibility.description: Definition lists (<dl>) must only contain valid <dt> and <dd> elements.

accessibility.title: Use correct list structure
accessibility.description: Lists (ul, ol) should only contain list item elements (li) to ensure they are correctly interpreted by assistive technology.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The ul element
HTML Living Standard: The ol element

accessibility.title: Use exactly one main landmark
accessibility.description: Each page must have one and only one main landmark.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The main element

accessibility.title: Use inclusive language
accessibility.description: Content uses inclusive, non-discriminatory language that welcomes all users regardless of ability, gender, race, or background.

accessibility.title: Use landmark regions correctly
accessibility.description: Proper landmark regions (main, nav, footer) help users navigate the page more efficiently.

accessibility.title: Use only allowed ARIA attributes for each role
accessibility.description: Checks that ARIA attributes are allowed on their elements to ensure valid accessibility trees.

accessibility.title: Use semantic list elements
accessibility.description: Groups of related items use ul, ol, or dl elements so screen readers announce list context and item count.

accessibility.title: Use semantic table markup for screen readers
accessibility.description: Data tables use proper semantic markup with headers, captions, and scope attributes for screen reader accessibility.

accessibility.title: Use valid ARIA role values
accessibility.description: Checks for valid ARIA role values

accessibility.title: Use valid values for ARIA attributes
accessibility.description: Checks for valid values in ARIA attributes

accessibility.title: Wrap definition items in a definition list
accessibility.description: Description terms (<dt>) and details (<dd>) must be contained within a <dl> element.

accessibility.title: Write in plain language
accessibility.description: Content uses clear, simple language that is easy to understand for users with cognitive disabilities and non-native speakers.

accessibility.title: Avoid autofocus on form fields
accessibility.description: Form fields do not use the autofocus attribute which can disorient screen reader users and cause unexpected page behavior.

accessibility.title: Avoid images of text
accessibility.description: Real text is used instead of images containing text, except for logos or when specific visual presentation is essential.

accessibility.title: Avoid redundant image alternative text
accessibility.description: Alternative text should not contain redundant words like 'image' or 'photo'.

documentation.title: W3C WAI Images Tutorial: Alternative Text

accessibility.title: Provide instant anchor scroll option
accessibility.description: Smooth scroll animations to anchor links respect motion preferences or provide an instant alternative.

css.title: Avoid embedded and inline CSS
css.description: Embedded and inline CSS are avoided except for critical CSS and performance optimization.

css.title: Inline critical CSS for faster rendering
css.description: Critical CSS (above-the-fold content) is inlined in the head for faster initial render.

css.title: Keep CSS specificity low and flat
css.description: Write selectors at the lowest specificity that works, avoiding ID selectors and deep nesting, so styles can be overridden cleanly without resorting to !important.

css.title: Load CSS without blocking render
css.description: Non-critical CSS is loaded asynchronously to avoid blocking DOM rendering.

css.title: Minify all CSS files
css.description: All CSS files are minified to reduce file size and improve page load performance.

css.title: Provide visible custom focus indicators
css.description: Ensure all interactive elements have a clearly visible focus indicator for keyboard navigation — never just remove the default outline without providing a better alternative.

css.title: Remove unused CSS rules
css.description: Unused CSS is removed to reduce bundle size and improve performance.

css.title: Use CSS custom properties for design tokens
css.description: Define design system values (colors, spacing, typography) as CSS custom properties on :root to enable consistent theming, dynamic updates, and dark mode support.

css.title: Use relative units for responsive layouts
css.description: Use rem, em, %, vw, vh, and clamp() instead of fixed px values to build layouts that scale with user font size preferences and viewport dimensions.

css.title: Use transform and opacity for animations
css.description: Animate with CSS transform and opacity properties to keep animations running on the GPU compositor thread at 60fps, avoiding layout-triggering properties like top, left, width, and height.

css.title: Apply Flexbox best practices
css.description: Use Flexbox for one-dimensional layouts with the right properties, avoiding common mistakes like overusing flex:1, ignoring min-width:0, and misunderstanding flex-basis.

css.title: Avoid intrusive interstitials
css.description: Full-screen interstitials (pop-ups, overlays, cookie banners) that block the main content on mobile are a ranking penalty signal and accessibility barrier.

documentation.title: Google: Intrusive Interstitials in Mobile Search

css.title: Include a print stylesheet
css.description: A print stylesheet is provided and correctly optimized for printed pages.

css.title: Lint CSS and SCSS files
css.description: All CSS/SCSS files are linted with Stylelint to detect errors and enforce standards.

css.title: Optimize web font formats
css.description: Web fonts use modern formats (WOFF2, WOFF) with proper fallbacks and loading strategies.

css.title: Order CSS files correctly
css.description: All CSS files are loaded before JavaScript files to prevent render blocking.

css.title: Prevent horizontal scrolling
css.description: Web pages must not require horizontal scrolling at standard viewport widths.
css.detail: Horizontal overflow breaks responsive layouts and makes content inaccessible to low-vision users who zoom in.

documentation.title: Google web.dev: Responsive web design basics

css.title: Support dark mode with prefers-color-scheme
css.description: Implement dark mode using the prefers-color-scheme media query and CSS custom properties so the site automatically adapts to the user's system preference.

css.title: Use a CSS reset or normalize stylesheet
css.description: A CSS reset or normalize is used to ensure consistent styling across browsers.

css.title: Use consistent CSS naming conventions
css.description: Adopt a consistent class naming methodology (BEM, CUBE CSS, or a team-agreed pattern) to make class names self-documenting and prevent style conflicts.

css.title: Use container queries for component-level responsiveness
css.description: Use CSS container queries to make components respond to their own container's size rather than the viewport, enabling truly reusable responsive components.

css.title: Use CSS containment to limit repaint scope
css.description: Apply the contain property to components to tell the browser they are independent from the rest of the page, enabling rendering optimizations that reduce repaint and reflow scope.

css.title: Use CSS Grid for two-dimensional layouts
css.description: Use CSS Grid when you need to control both rows and columns simultaneously, such as page layouts, card grids, and complex component arrangements.

css.title: Use CSS logical properties for i18n and RTL support
css.description: Use CSS logical properties (margin-inline, padding-block, border-inline-start) instead of physical properties (margin-left, padding-top) to support right-to-left languages automatically.

css.title: Use readable font sizes on mobile
css.description: Text must be large enough to read without zooming on mobile devices.
css.detail: Using relative units (rem/em) allows browser font size preferences to be respected.

css.title: Register CSS custom properties with @property for animation and type safety
css.description: Use @property to register CSS custom properties with a type, initial value, and inheritance control — enabling animation of custom properties and providing compile-time validation for design tokens.

css.title: Use :has() to style parent elements based on their descendants
css.description: Use the CSS :has() relational pseudo-class to select and style an element based on what it contains, replacing JavaScript DOM manipulation for many common styling scenarios.

documentation.title: Chrome for Developers: :has(): the family selector

css.title: Use @layer to manage CSS cascade order explicitly
css.description: CSS Cascade Layers (@layer) are used to give the codebase explicit, predictable control over specificity and cascade order, eliminating the need to fight specificity with !important.

documentation.title: Chrome for Developers: Cascade layers are coming to your browser
CSS Tricks: A Complete Guide to CSS Cascade Layers

css.title: Use CSS subgrid to align nested grid items to parent tracks
css.description: Use grid-template-columns: subgrid (or subgrid for rows) to make nested grid items participate in the parent grid's tracks, solving the card-content alignment problem without JavaScript height matching.

css.title: Use oklch() and oklab() for perceptually uniform colour palettes
css.description: Colour values in the design system use oklch() or oklab() colour functions to produce perceptually uniform palettes where equal numeric steps produce equal perceived lightness changes.

css.title: Use the View Transitions API for smooth page and component transitions
css.description: The View Transitions API is used to animate between page states or navigations with cross-fade or custom animations, providing a native-app quality transition without JavaScript animation libraries.

documentation.title: web.dev: Smooth transitions with the View Transitions API

head.title: X-UA-Compatible
head.description: The X-UA-Compatible Meta tag is present.

head.title: Favicons
head.description: Each favicon has been created and displays correctly.
head.detail: If you have only a favicon.ico, put it at the root of your site. Normally you won't need to use any markup. However, it's still good practice to link to it using the example below. Today, PNG format is recommended over .ico format (dimensions: 32x32px).

documentation.title: Favicons, Touch Icons, Tile Icons, etc. Which Do You Need? - CSS Tricks

head.title: Windows Tiles
head.description: Windows tiles are present and linked.

head.title: Canonical
head.description: Use rel="canonical" to avoid duplicate content.

documentation.title: Use canonical URLs - Search Console Help - Google Support
5 common mistakes with rel=canonical - Google Webmaster Blog

head.title: Alternate language
head.description: The language tag of your website is specified and related to the language of the current page.

head.title: Conditional comments
head.description: Conditional comments are present for IE if needed.

documentation.title: About conditional comments (Internet Explorer) - MSDN - Microsoft

head.title: RSS feed
head.description: If your project is a blog or has articles, an RSS link was provided.

head.title: CSS order
head.description: All CSS files are loaded before any JavaScript files in the HEAD
head.detail: (Except the case where sometimes JS files are loaded asynchronously on top of your page)

head.title: Facebook Open Graph
head.detail: All Facebook Open Graph (OG) are tested and no one is missing or with a false information. Images need to be at least 600 x 315 pixels, although 1200 x 630 pixels is recommended. Using og:image:width and og:image:height will specify the image dimensions to the crawler so that it can render the image immediately without having to asynchronously download and process it.

documentation.title: A Guide to Sharing for Webmasters

tools.title: Test your page with the Facebook OG testing

documentation.title: Getting started with cards — Twitter Developers

tools.title: Test your page with the Twitter card validator

html.title: Declare UTF-8 character encoding
html.description: The charset (UTF-8) is declared correctly as the first element in the head.

html.title: Set the responsive viewport meta tag
html.description: The viewport meta tag is declared correctly for responsive design.

html.title: Use the HTML5 doctype
html.description: The HTML5 doctype declaration must appear as the first line of every HTML document to trigger standards mode rendering in all browsers.

documentation.title: MDN: Quirks Mode and Standards Mode

html.title: Add Subresource Integrity to external scripts
html.description: Use Subresource Integrity (SRI) hash attributes on external scripts and stylesheets loaded from CDNs to ensure the content hasn't been tampered with.

html.title: Analyze performance with WebPageTest
html.description: Page performance is analyzed with WebPageTest to identify loading bottlenecks and optimization opportunities.

html.title: Ensure all IDs are unique
html.description: All ID attributes are unique within the document.
html.detail: No duplicate IDs exist on the page.

html.title: Load scripts with defer, async, or type=module
html.description: Prevent JavaScript from blocking HTML parsing by using defer, async, or type=module attributes on script tags so the browser can continue building the DOM while scripts download.

html.title: Make notifications accessible
html.description: Toast notifications and alerts are announced to screen readers using ARIA live regions and appropriate roles.

html.title: Make videos accessible with captions
html.description: Videos have captions, audio descriptions, transcripts, pause controls, and avoid autoplay for users with hearing, vision, or cognitive impairments.

documentation.title: WebAIM: Captions, Transcripts, and Audio Descriptions

html.title: Set the page lang attribute
html.description: The <html> element must have a lang attribute with a valid BCP 47 language code so screen readers, translation tools, and search engines know the primary language of the page.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The lang attribute

html.title: Use navigation landmark regions
html.description: Page navigation uses nav elements with proper ARIA labels to distinguish multiple navigation regions.

html.title: Use semantic HTML elements
html.description: HTML5 Semantic Elements are used appropriately (header, section, footer, main, article, aside...).

html.title: Use semantic input type attributes
html.description: Set the correct type attribute on input elements to trigger the right mobile keyboard, enable browser validation, and improve autofill accuracy.

html.title: Validate forms accessibly
html.description: Forms provide clear validation feedback with accessible error messages and proper ARIA attributes.

html.title: Validate HTML against W3C standards
html.description: HTML markup is validated against W3C standards for cross-browser compatibility.

html.title: Add thumbnail images to videos
html.description: HTML5 video elements should have a poster attribute providing a thumbnail image displayed before the video loads or is played.

documentation.title: HTML Living Standard: The video element — poster attribute

html.title: Check for broken links
html.description: All links are tested and none are broken.

html.title: Create a custom 404 error page
html.description: A custom 404 error page is designed with helpful navigation options for lost users.

html.title: Create accessible tooltips
html.description: Tooltips are accessible to keyboard users and screen readers with proper ARIA attributes and focus handling.

html.title: Implement accessible breadcrumb navigation
html.description: Breadcrumb navigation is implemented with proper semantic markup and ARIA attributes for accessibility.

html.title: Implement favicons for all devices
html.description: All necessary favicon formats are implemented for browsers, devices, and PWA support.

html.title: Link a Web App Manifest for installability
html.description: Include a Web App Manifest (manifest.json) linked from the HTML head to enable Progressive Web App features like home screen installation, standalone display, and splash screens.

html.title: Make accordions keyboard navigable
html.description: Accordion components use proper ARIA attributes and keyboard interactions for screen reader accessibility.

html.title: Make carousels accessible
html.description: Carousels and sliders are accessible with pause controls, keyboard navigation, and proper ARIA attributes.

html.title: Make custom elements and Web Components accessible
html.description: Custom elements must implement ARIA reflection via ElementInternals, keyboard interaction, and form association so that screen readers and assistive technologies can interpret them correctly.

html.title: Make drag and drop accessible
html.description: Drag and drop interfaces provide keyboard alternatives and proper ARIA attributes for accessibility.

html.title: Make file uploads accessible
html.description: File upload components are accessible with proper labels, file type restrictions, and progress feedback.

html.title: Make pagination accessible
html.description: Pagination controls are accessible with proper ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and current page indication.

html.title: Make search inputs accessible
html.description: Search functionality is accessible with proper input type, label, role, and autocomplete suggestions.

html.title: Make tabs keyboard navigable
html.description: Tab components implement the ARIA tabs pattern with proper roles, states, and keyboard navigation.

html.title: Provide noscript fallback content
html.description: A noscript tag provides fallback content for users with JavaScript disabled.

html.title: Remove comments and debug code in production
html.description: Unnecessary code, comments, and debug elements are removed before deploying to production.

html.title: Set text direction for RTL languages
html.description: The dir attribute is used for languages that read right-to-left (RTL) or mixed content.

html.title: Meet PWA installability criteria
html.description: The web app satisfies the browser's minimum PWA installability requirements: a valid web app manifest, a registered service worker, HTTPS, and maskable icons.

documentation.title: web.dev: What makes a good Progressive Web App?
web.dev: Add a web app manifest

i18n.title: Add hreflang tags for multilingual sites
i18n.description: Hreflang tags indicate language and regional variations for multilingual sites.

i18n.title: Design UI components to accommodate text expansion from translation
i18n.description: Ensure that layouts use flexible sizing so that translated text — which can be 30–50% longer than English — does not overflow, clip, or break the UI.

documentation.title: W3C Internationalization: Text size in translation

i18n.title: Handle plural forms with Intl.PluralRules or ICU MessageFormat
i18n.description: Select the correct grammatical plural category for every language using Intl.PluralRules or an ICU-aware i18n library instead of simple singular/plural branching.

i18n.title: Use Intl APIs for currency, number, and date formatting
i18n.description: Format monetary values, numbers, and dates using the browser's built-in Intl.NumberFormat and Intl.DateTimeFormat APIs instead of manual string manipulation.

i18n.title: Use locale-neutral images and provide cultural overrides when needed
i18n.description: Default to abstract, culture-neutral icons and illustrations, and supply locale-specific image variants only when visual content carries meaning that differs across regions.

documentation.title: Nielsen Norman Group: Culturally Responsive Design

images.title: Provide meaningful alt text for images
images.description: Every informative image has a descriptive alt attribute; decorative images use alt="" to be ignored by screen readers.

images.title: Compress images without quality loss
images.description: All images are compressed without significant quality loss to reduce file sizes.

images.title: Fix broken images
images.description: No images return 404 errors or display broken-image icons to users.

images.title: Implement responsive images with srcset
images.description: Images use srcset and sizes attributes for responsive delivery across devices.

images.title: Keep image file sizes within recommended limits
images.description: Individual image files are compressed to reasonable sizes to avoid wasted bandwidth and slow load times, especially on mobile networks.

images.title: Lazy load offscreen images
images.description: Images below the visible viewport use loading="lazy" to defer download until the user scrolls near them, reducing initial page load time.

images.title: Optimise images for faster loading
images.description: All images are compressed and metadata-stripped before deployment, removing unnecessary bytes without visible quality loss.

images.title: Optimize all images for web
images.description: Images are optimized with appropriate formats, compression, and modern techniques.

images.title: Prioritize loading critical images
images.description: Hero and above-the-fold images are preloaded with high fetch priority for LCP.

images.title: Serve images at the correct display size
images.description: Images are not significantly larger than their display dimensions—serving a 2000px image for a 400px container wastes bandwidth and hurts LCP.

images.title: Serve images from a CDN
images.description: Images are served from a CDN with automatic optimization, resizing, and format conversion.

images.title: Set explicit width and height on images
images.description: All elements have explicit width and height attributes so browsers can reserve space before the image loads, preventing layout shift.

images.title: Use with an fallback
images.description: Every element contains a required fallback as its last child, ensuring images display in all browsers including those that don't support .

images.title: Use modern image formats (WebP, AVIF)
images.description: Images are served in modern formats (WebP or AVIF) instead of legacy JPEG/PNG where browser support allows, reducing file size without visible quality loss.

images.title: Use srcset for responsive images
images.description: Images wider than 100px use the srcset attribute to offer multiple resolution variants, letting the browser download the optimal size for the user's viewport and device pixel ratio.

images.title: Use WebP format with fallbacks
images.description: Images are served in WebP format with fallbacks for older browsers.

images.title: Manage inline SVG size and complexity
images.description: Large or complex SVGs inlined in HTML are extracted to external files or components, preventing them from bloating the HTML document and blocking parsing.

images.title: Optimize SVG files
images.description: SVG files are optimized with SVGO to remove unnecessary metadata and reduce size.

images.title: Support high-DPI retina displays
images.description: High-resolution images (2x, 3x) are provided for retina and high-DPI displays.

images.title: Use <figure> and <figcaption> for image captions
images.description: Images with visible captions are wrapped in <figure> with a <figcaption> child, creating a semantic association between image and caption.

images.title: Use AVIF format for modern browsers
images.description: Images support AVIF format for superior compression with proper browser fallbacks.

images.title: Handle image loading errors gracefully
images.description: Broken images are handled gracefully with fallback images or placeholder content.

images.title: Use descriptive image filenames
images.description: Image filenames are descriptive and human-readable, using lowercase letters, hyphens as separators, and meaningful words that reflect the image content.

images.title: Use image sprites where appropriate
images.description: Small images and icons use sprites or SVG to reduce HTTP requests.

images.title: Use progressive JPEG encoding
images.description: JPEG images use progressive format for better perceived loading performance.

javascript.title: Never use eval() or unsafe dynamic code execution
javascript.description: Avoid eval(), new Function(), setTimeout/setInterval with string arguments, and innerHTML with untrusted content — they execute arbitrary code and create critical XSS vulnerabilities.

javascript.title: Avoid inline JavaScript
javascript.description: Inline JavaScript is avoided.
javascript.detail: JavaScript is kept in external files for caching and maintainability.

javascript.title: Debounce and throttle event handlers
javascript.description: Use debounce or throttle for high-frequency events like scroll, resize, and input to improve performance.

javascript.title: Enable TypeScript strict mode in tsconfig.json
javascript.description: Enable "strict": true in tsconfig.json to activate the full suite of TypeScript type-checking flags and catch the most common runtime bugs at compile time.

documentation.title: TypeScript: Do not use the default tsconfig

javascript.title: Handle cross-origin requests securely
javascript.description: Use CORS correctly, validate message origins with postMessage, and understand the Same-Origin Policy to prevent cross-origin attacks.

javascript.title: Implement proper error handling
javascript.description: Use try-catch blocks and error boundaries to gracefully handle errors in async operations and UI components.

javascript.title: Minify all JavaScript files
javascript.description: All JavaScript files are minified to reduce file size and improve loading performance.

javascript.title: Minimize costly DOM read/write operations
javascript.description: Batch DOM reads and writes separately to avoid layout thrashing — the performance problem caused by alternating between reading and writing layout properties.

javascript.title: Prefer const and let over var
javascript.description: Use block-scoped const and let declarations instead of function-scoped var to avoid hoisting bugs and unintended variable mutations.

javascript.title: Prevent common memory leak patterns
javascript.description: Identify and avoid the most common JavaScript memory leak sources: forgotten event listeners, retained DOM references, closures holding large objects, and uncleared timers.

javascript.title: Split large JavaScript bundles
javascript.description: Use dynamic imports and route-based code splitting to break large bundles into smaller chunks that load on demand, reducing initial page load time.

documentation.title: web.dev: Code splitting with dynamic imports in Next.js

javascript.title: Use ES modules (import/export)
javascript.description: Use native ES module syntax for imports and exports instead of CommonJS require() to enable static analysis, tree-shaking, and better tooling support.

javascript.title: Validate external data at runtime with a schema library
javascript.description: Use Zod or Valibot to validate data from API responses, form inputs, localStorage, and environment variables — TypeScript types are erased at runtime and cannot protect against unexpected shapes.

javascript.title: Avoid implicit type coercion
javascript.description: Use strict equality (===), explicit type conversion, and Number/String/Boolean constructors to avoid JavaScript's implicit type coercion producing unexpected results.

javascript.title: Avoid the any type — use unknown, generics, or type guards instead
javascript.description: Replace TypeScript's any type with unknown, proper generics, or narrowed type assertions to preserve type safety without sacrificing expressiveness.

javascript.title: Enable noUncheckedIndexedAccess to catch out-of-bounds array bugs
javascript.description: Enable noUncheckedIndexedAccess in tsconfig.json to make array and object index access return T | undefined, forcing explicit null checks that prevent out-of-bounds runtime errors.

documentation.title: TypeScript 4.1 Release Notes: Checked Indexed Accesses

javascript.title: Lint JavaScript code
javascript.description: JavaScript code is linted with ESLint to detect errors and enforce coding standards.

javascript.title: Parse JSON safely with error handling
javascript.description: Always wrap JSON.parse() in try/catch and validate the parsed structure before use, as invalid JSON or unexpected data shapes cause runtime errors.

javascript.title: Prefer immutable data patterns
javascript.description: Use spread operators, Object.assign, and array methods that return new values instead of mutating objects and arrays in place, to make data flow predictable and debugging easier.

javascript.title: Remove console statements in production
javascript.description: Remove or disable console.log, console.debug, and other console statements before deploying to production.

javascript.title: Use event delegation for dynamic content
javascript.description: Attach event listeners to stable parent elements rather than individual dynamic children to reduce memory usage and handle elements added to the DOM after page load.

javascript.title: Use modern array and object methods
javascript.description: Use ES2015+ array methods (map, filter, reduce, find, flatMap) and object methods (Object.entries, Object.fromEntries, structuredClone) for cleaner, more expressive code.

javascript.title: Use scheduler.yield() to keep the main thread responsive during long tasks
javascript.description: Break up tasks longer than 50 ms by yielding to the browser with scheduler.yield() or a MessageChannel fallback so that user input is never blocked.

javascript.title: Use Web Storage API safely
javascript.description: Use localStorage and sessionStorage with proper serialization, error handling, and security awareness to avoid data corruption and storage quota errors.

javascript.title: Write internationalisation-friendly translation strings
javascript.description: Translation strings use message format patterns (ICU or similar) rather than string concatenation, and correctly handle pluralisation, gender, and variable interpolation.

javascript.title: Use import type for type-only imports
javascript.description: Use the import type syntax for imports that are only needed as TypeScript types, ensuring they are fully erased at compile time with zero runtime cost.

performance.title: Optimize largest contentful paint
performance.description: The largest content element loads within 2.5 seconds for a good user experience.

performance.title: Enable browser caching
performance.description: Cache-Control and ETag headers are properly configured for static resources.

performance.title: Enable HTTP/2 or HTTP/3
performance.description: Use modern HTTP protocols to enable request multiplexing and reduce network latency.

performance.title: Enable text-based compression
performance.description: Compress text resources (HTML, CSS, JS) using Gzip or Brotli to reduce data transfer size.

performance.title: Implement Google Consent Mode v2
performance.description: Adjust Google Tag behavior based on user consent to comply with privacy regulations and maintain data insights.

performance.title: Implement lazy loading for offscreen content
performance.description: Images and heavy resources below the fold are lazy loaded to improve initial performance.

performance.title: Keep page load time under 3 seconds
performance.description: Page fully loads in under 3 seconds on a standard connection.

performance.title: Keep page weight under 1500KB
performance.description: Total page weight including all resources is under 1500KB (ideally under 500KB).

performance.title: Load non-critical code on user interaction
performance.description: Defer JavaScript modules, widgets, and third-party code until the user signals intent through a click, focus, hover, or similar interaction.

documentation.title: web.dev: Code splitting with dynamic imports in Next.js

performance.title: Load non-critical code when content approaches the viewport
performance.description: Use viewport-aware loading to fetch components, embeds, and feature code shortly before they become visible instead of shipping them on first load.

performance.title: Minimize critical request chains
performance.description: Reduce the number and depth of dependent resource requests that block the initial rendering of the page.

performance.title: Minimize cumulative layout shift
performance.description: Page maintains visual stability with a CLS score below 0.1, preventing unexpected content shifts during load.

performance.title: Minimize HTTP requests
performance.description: HTTP requests are minimized by combining files, using sprites, and HTTP/2.

performance.title: Optimize and compress web videos
performance.description: Videos are compressed, resized per device, and served in efficient codecs (H.264, HEVC, VP9/AV1) to reduce page weight and bandwidth use.

performance.title: Optimize first contentful paint
performance.description: First content renders within 1.8 seconds, providing quick visual feedback that the page is loading.

performance.title: Optimize interaction to next paint
performance.description: Page responds to user interactions within 200ms, ensuring good responsiveness.

performance.title: Optimize pages for back/forward cache
performance.description: Pages avoid back/forward cache blockers such as unload listeners and restore state correctly when a browser resumes them from memory.

performance.title: Optimize third-party script loading
performance.description: Load third-party scripts asynchronously to prevent blocking the main thread and improve page performance.

performance.title: Optimize web font loading
performance.description: Use efficient font formats and loading strategies to prevent layout shifts and invisible text.

performance.title: Show loading indicators
performance.description: Loading indicators provide feedback during asynchronous operations to keep users informed of progress.

performance.title: Use a content delivery network
performance.description: Static assets are served from a CDN for reduced latency and faster delivery.

performance.title: Use resource hints for faster loading
performance.description: Implement preload, prefetch, and preconnect hints to optimize resource loading priority.

performance.title: Virtualize long lists and tables
performance.description: Render only the visible subset of rows or cards in large collections to reduce DOM size, memory usage, and scroll-time rendering work.

documentation.title: web.dev: Virtualize large lists with react-window

performance.title: Avoid JavaScript-based redirects
performance.description: Detects JavaScript resources that return 3XX redirects to reduce latency

performance.title: Avoid serving legacy JavaScript to modern browsers
performance.description: Detects ES5 polyfills and legacy JavaScript code to reduce bundle size and improve execution

performance.title: Convert animated GIFs to video
performance.description: Large animated GIFs are replaced with more efficient video formats like MP4 or WebM to reduce page weight.

performance.title: Disable lazy loading for above-the-fold content
performance.description: Detects lazy loading on likely above-fold images to improve Largest Contentful Paint (LCP)

performance.title: Eliminate render-blocking resources
performance.description: Checks for render-blocking CSS and JavaScript that prevent the initial page render

performance.title: Optimize CSS file size
performance.description: Keep individual CSS files small and remove unused styles to accelerate the critical rendering path.

performance.title: Optimize Google Tag Manager implementation
performance.description: Configure Google Tag Manager efficiently to minimize its impact on page load speed and main-thread blocking.

performance.title: Optimize JavaScript bundle size
performance.description: Checks for JavaScript files that exceed recommended size limits to ensure fast interaction

performance.title: Perform browser-based performance audits
performance.description: Conduct performance audits in a full browser environment to capture accurate runtime metrics and layout shifts.

performance.title: Provide source maps for production debugging
performance.description: Checks for source map availability and configuration to ensure easier debugging

performance.title: Reduce DOM size and complexity
performance.description: Keep the DOM tree small and shallow to improve memory usage and rendering performance.

performance.title: Reduce Time to First Byte (TTFB)
performance.description: Measures and optimizes server response time (TTFB) to ensure a fast initial response

performance.title: Register a service worker for caching and offline support
performance.description: A service worker is registered to intercept network requests, cache critical assets, and enable offline functionality for your web application.

performance.title: Remove duplicate JavaScript libraries
performance.description: Detect and consolidate duplicate JavaScript libraries to reduce bundle size and prevent version conflicts.

performance.title: Stream HTML to the browser before the full response is ready
performance.description: Use HTTP chunked transfer encoding and React renderToPipeableStream (or ReadableStream) to begin delivering HTML to the browser as soon as the first bytes are available, reducing Time to First Byte and First Contentful Paint.

documentation.title: web.dev: Streaming requests with the Fetch API

performance.title: Use fetchpriority to hint resource loading priority
performance.description: The fetchpriority attribute is applied to critical images, scripts, and preload links to help the browser prioritise the most important resources and defer lower-priority ones.

documentation.title: web.dev: Optimise resource loading with the Fetch Priority API

performance.title: Use preconnect for critical third-party origins
performance.description: Checks for preconnect hints to critical third-party origins to reduce connection latency

performance.title: Use secure and up-to-date JS libraries
performance.description: Detects JavaScript libraries and checks for known vulnerabilities

performance.title: Provide an offline fallback page
performance.description: When the network is unavailable, users are shown a custom offline fallback page rather than the browser's generic error screen.

documentation.title: web.dev: Create an offline fallback page

performance.title: Use the Speculation Rules API to prefetch and prerender navigations
performance.description: The Speculation Rules API is used to declaratively prefetch or prerender likely next pages, making navigation feel near-instant without the overhead of a full client-side router.

privacy.title: Link to your privacy policy in the footer
privacy.description: Websites that collect any personal data must publish a privacy policy and link to it prominently — this is a legal requirement under GDPR, CCPA, and most other privacy regulations.

privacy.title: Avoid third-party cookies

privacy.detail: Modern browsers are phasing them out, and regulations like GDPR and CCPA require consent before setting them.

documentation.title: web.dev: Preparing for the end of third-party cookies

security.title: Leaked Environment Variables

security.title: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
security.description: All HTTP requests must be permanently redirected (301) to HTTPS to prevent users from accessing your site over an insecure connection.

security.title: Serve all pages over HTTPS
security.description: Every page and resource on your site must be delivered over HTTPS to protect user data in transit and enable modern browser features.

security.title: Submit forms over HTTPS
security.description: All HTML form actions must point to HTTPS URLs to ensure form data is encrypted in transit and cannot be intercepted by network attackers.

security.title: Audit dependencies for known vulnerabilities
security.description: Dependencies are regularly scanned for known security vulnerabilities using automated tooling, and critical findings are remediated before deployment.

documentation.title: OWASP: A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components

security.title: Avoid mixed content on HTTPS pages
security.description: An HTTPS page that loads resources over HTTP has mixed content — browsers block or warn about these requests, breaking functionality and undermining transport security.

security.title: Implement a content security policy
security.description: A Content Security Policy is implemented to prevent XSS attacks and control resource loading.

security.title: Prevent stack trace exposure in production error responses
security.description: Production error responses never include stack traces, internal file paths, framework internals, or other debugging detail that could aid an attacker (OWASP A09).

documentation.title: OWASP: A09:2021 – Security Logging and Monitoring Failures

security.title: Secure password input fields
security.description: Password fields implement security best practices including proper autocomplete, show/hide toggle, and strength indicators.

security.title: Set an HSTS header
security.description: The Strict-Transport-Security response header tells browsers to always use HTTPS for your domain, preventing protocol downgrade attacks and cookie hijacking.

documentation.title: OWASP: HTTP Strict Transport Security Cheat Sheet

security.title: Set an X-Frame-Options header
security.description: The X-Frame-Options header controls whether your page can be embedded in an iframe, frame, or object — preventing clickjacking attacks.

security.title: Set Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite flags on session cookies
security.description: All session and authentication cookies are issued with the Secure, HttpOnly, and an appropriate SameSite flag to prevent interception, JavaScript exfiltration, and cross-site request forgery.

security.title: Set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
security.description: The X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header prevents browsers from MIME-sniffing a response away from the declared Content-Type, blocking a class of drive-by download and XSS attacks.

security.title: Store authentication tokens securely
security.description: Sensitive authentication tokens are stored in httpOnly cookies rather than localStorage or sessionStorage to prevent theft via cross-site scripting attacks (OWASP A07).

documentation.title: OWASP: A07:2021 – Identification and Authentication Failures

security.title: External Link Security
security.description: Links that open in a new tab using target='_blank' must include rel='noopener noreferrer' to prevent the opened page from accessing the opener's window context.

documentation.title: OWASP WSTG: Testing for Reverse Tabnabbing

security.title: Link to your terms of service in the footer
security.description: Websites offering services to users should publish Terms of Service and link to them from every page — this establishes the legal agreement governing use of the service.

documentation.title: GDPR Article 13 - Information to be provided where personal data collected from the data subject

security.title: Protect public forms with CAPTCHA

security.title: Set a Permissions-Policy header
security.description: The Permissions-Policy header lets servers restrict which browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, etc.) can be used in a page or its embedded iframes.

security.title: Set a Referrer-Policy header

security.title: Use COOP, COEP, and CORP for cross-origin isolation when needed

audit.TITLE: Audit a live page
audit.LEAD: Paste a public URL and we'll run up to 246 automatic checks against it. You get a score, what to fix, and one click to tick the passing items in your checklist.
audit.LABEL: Page URL
audit.APPLY: Tick passing items in my checklist
audit.NOTE: Automatic checks cover only what can be verified from the page's HTML and response headers. Everything else, such as real-device testing or content quality, stays a manual item in the checklist. Only public pages can be audited.
audit.BRAND_TAGLINE: Websites, web apps and engineering support
audit.BRAND_CTA: Need help fixing these issues? Talk to Shinning Tech Services
audit.REPORT_DISCLAIMER: This is an automated, point-in-time scan of one public page. It reads the page's HTML, linked CSS/JS, images and response headers. It is a starting point for a review, not a certification, and it does not replace manual testing.
audit.HEURISTIC_NOTE: Items marked “verify” rely on heuristics (for example reading level, minification, thin content or script detection) and can be false positives or negatives. Confirm them manually before acting.
LIMITS: Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP) and other real-user or lab performance metrics. Only server response time, page weight and loading hints are checked.
Real-device, browser and screen-reader testing, and visual quality (layout, colour contrast in context, animation).
Content quality, tone, accuracy and legal wording. Only simple signals such as length and reading level are estimated.
Pages behind a login, forms, checkout and other interactive flows. Only the public page you submitted is fetched, with no JavaScript execution.
The Testing section of the checklist (unit, end-to-end, visual and load tests live in your codebase, not on the page).
Only one page is scanned; other pages of the site may differ.
audit.NOT_CHECKED_INTRO: Checklist items this scan did not decide. Review these manually:

help.TITLE: How to use this checklist
help.INTRO: A front-end quality checklist you can work through by hand or partly automate.

STEPS.title: 1. Work through the checklist.
STEPS.text: Open a section from the sidebar and tick items as you complete them. Click the arrow on an item for documentation and tools.

STEPS.title: 2. Filter what matters.
STEPS.text: Use the tag pills to focus on one area, and the eye icon to hide a section you don't need.

STEPS.title: 3. Audit a live page.
STEPS.text: On the Audit page, paste a URL. Up to 246 checks run automatically and the passing items can be ticked in your checklist in one click.

STEPS.title: 4. Generate a report.
STEPS.text: Open Report to fill in the project name and developer, then print or save a PDF of your progress.

TIPS: Your progress is saved in this browser only. Nothing is uploaded.
The dark/light button remembers your choice.
Use EN / FR in the top bar to switch language.
AI assistants can run the audit too: see the MCP server and agent skill in the GitHub repository.
